# smart-clowes-clark-2025-chatgpt-extended
- **URL:** https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/s11229-025-05046-y (publisher-deposited metadata and abstract) ; publisher page https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11229-025-05046-y returned a bot "Client Challenge" to every fetch; ePrints Soton, PhilPapers and Sussex Figshare copies all returned 403 · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v1 drafting, claim C15
- **What it establishes:** Paul Smart, Robert Clowes & Andy Clark, "ChatGPT, extended: large language models and the extended mind," *Synthese* 205(6), article 242 (published 6 June 2025), doi 10.1007/s11229-025-05046-y, CC BY. Authors, title, journal, DOI confirmed from the DOI registration. I read only the abstract, not the body. Important scope note: the paper is about whether an *LLM* (a retrieval-augmented "Digital Andy") is itself an extended cognitive/computational system; it is not primarily a paper about humans extending their minds with ChatGPT.
- **Key passages:** "Applying this technique to the works of the contemporary philosopher Andy Clark yields Digital Andy: an LLM that is able to respond to questions about the extended mind." / "But Digital Andy's reliance on extra-systemic resources also raises questions about the scope of active externalist theorizing, encouraging us to consider Digital Andy's status as an extended cognitive/computational system." / "some interesting points of convergence between the philosophical effort to understand the extended mind and the technological effort to build the next generation of LLMs."
- **Reliability:** Primary metadata (Crossref deposit by Springer); abstract only. Peer-reviewed philosophy journal.
- **Relevance to this project:** C15. Safe to cite as "exists; Clark and colleagues have begun applying the extended-mind framework to LLMs." Do not cite it as evidence that ChatGPT extends *users'* minds; that is not what the abstract claims.
